title: Atlantic City Follies with Marva Louis, then Philadelphia and New York clubs
summary: The Davis band toured with the Atlantic City Follies featuring Marva Louis and Peg Leg Bates, then played Philadelphia from December and a New York club until June 1946.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No, not quite two years. I stayed up there with him all that year, and then I left... We left there and went out on the road with a show called Atlantic City Follies. That was with Peg Leg Bates and Marva Louis, Joe Louis' wife -

- it was featuring her. Naturally, at the time she was just going on Joe's name. Because she couldn't do nothin'. Shit, she couldn't sing. She was just pretty, thousand dollar gowns and all that stuff. In those days women wanted to see her. "I'm going to see Marva Louis. I want to see one of them pretty gowns she has? Did you see her last night?" We played the Howard Theatre. We traveled all over with her, with that show.

When that show was over, when we got off the road, we went to Philadelphia, and stayed at Philadelphia three months at a club called Shangalai(?) Club. We went there, and we stayed there for... Marva wasn't with the show then. She'd left. We stayed up there from December until March.

Then after we left there, we went to New York and stayed in the Baron's Club -- stayed up there from March until June. Then we went back to Atlantic City in June. I'm still in '46. And that's where I left them.
